title: Mirabel and the Extraction
premise: Coral Quintana, a deniable fixer for an embassy that appears on no map, discovers her safe house listed on a real estate site — photographed room by room, down to the burner phones in the drawer. Someone inside the network sold her out, and the listing is a countdown: whoever closes the sale gets everything Coral has spent a decade hiding. Racing through Lisbon, Vienna, and Frankfurt, she must smuggle a witness and a ledger of sanctioned deals past three governments that all want them buried, pursued by an assassin who turns out to be the only other survivor of the program that made her. Coral ends the book by detonating her own legend — publishing the ledger herself, burning her identity to give the truth a life she can no longer protect or claim.
about_author: Petra Voss is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent six years auditing offshore shell companies before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about paper trails, plausible deniability, and the people who live inside them.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A routine dead-drop at a Lisbon café is interrupted when her handler sends a link: the safe house, photographed in loving detail, listed at a suspiciously fair price. Coral's calm professional detachment cracks as she recognizes the angle of the bedroom photo — taken from inside, from her bed. Beat: dread arriving in the shape of ordinary commerce.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Coral. She sweeps the safe house and catalogs what the photos revealed: the ledger's hiding place, the witness files, the emergency routes. Her junior colleague Ilse argues they report up; Coral knows the embassy that doesn't exist has no up. Beat: the loneliness of being the only person who can be trusted with yourself.

chapters.title: Three Calls, No Names
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Working her contacts, Coral triangulates which of three governments — German, Austrian, or her own shadow employer — ordered the listing as a soft extraction. Each call is coded, courteous, and a lie. Beat: the sickening realization that invisibility was always someone else's permission, not her achievement.

chapters.title: The Man Who Photographed Rooms
chapters.summary: POV Coral, then a short second-person interlude from the photographer. She traces the listing to a freelance real-estate photographer who doesn't remember taking the shots — his camera was borrowed, his memory of that day fogged by a lunch he can't account for. Beat: the horror of a professional machine that erases people without violence.

chapters.title: Ilse's Doubt
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The junior officer secretly copies Coral's contingency files, unsure whether Coral is the leak or the target. Ilse's chapters expose the embassy's banal bureaucracy — expense reports for kidnappings, performance reviews for silence. Beat: complicity dressed up as careerism.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The ledger she protects documents sanctioned weapons deals settling through Frankfurt on Monday morning. If it surfaces before the markets open, three governments lose deniability. If it doesn't, the witness dies quietly and the deals clear. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Résumé
chapters.summary: POV Miro, the assassin. Contracted to retrieve the ledger, Miro is methodical, courteous, and increasingly haunted — he recognizes Coral's tradecraft because they were trained by the same vanished program. Beat: a killer discovering his target is a mirror.

chapters.title: Vienna, Off the Books
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral moves the witness, Anselm, a disgraced banker, through Vienna using routes she built for people she never expected to be one of. Anselm is pathetic, funny, and genuinely guilty. Beat: the price of survival measured in the company you're forced to keep.

chapters.title: The Sale Falls Through
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The listing vanishes overnight — not withdrawn, erased from every archive, including Ilse's screenshots. Someone inside is cleaning as they go. Ilse confronts Coral; Coral lies badly for the first time in her career. Beat: trust fracturing exactly when it's needed most.

chapters.title: What the Program Made
chapters.summary: POV Miro. Miro's handlers feed him Coral's file, and he reads his own history in it — the orphanage, the language training, the first job at nineteen. He begins editing what he reports. Beat: the assassin choosing, one omission at a time, to become a person.

chapters.title: The Embassy That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral breaks into the embassy's nominal offices in Brussels and finds a floor of empty desks, a switchboard that rings nowhere, and her own personnel file: terminated, three years ago. She has been working for a ghost — and so has everyone hunting her. Beat: identity collapsing like a stage set.

chapters.title: Anselm's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Anselm. Hiding in a canal house, the banker records a confession he knows may be his eulogy, admitting he built the settlement structure and kept a copy of the ledger out of vanity, not conscience. Beat: cowardice and courage indistinguishable at this hour.

chapters.title: Interception on the A3
chapters.summary: POV Coral and Miro, alternating. A German intelligence team intercepts their car outside Frankfurt; Miro arrives to finish the job and instead kills the team's own tracker, saving Coral without explanation. Beat: the moment the hunter's cover story dies.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Room
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ilse is summoned to a joint session where German, Austrian, and her own handlers negotiate who takes custody of 'the Quintana problem' — she realizes she was promoted to be the fall. Beat: the machinery of justice outside the law, shown from the inside.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral offers Miro the ledger and her escape routes; he offers her the program's archive, which names every asset ever made — including her. They strike an uneasy alliance over a gas station meal neither tastes. Beat: two survivors discovering the price they both already paid.

chapters.title: Ilse's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. Ordered to plant false evidence framing Coral as the leak, Ilse instead uploads the embassy's internal correspondence to Coral's dead-drop. She knows what it costs. Beat: a minor character choosing to be a major one.

chapters.title: Night Before the Market
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In a Frankfurt hotel, Coral prepares two versions of Monday: the quiet one where the ledger dies with her, and the loud one. Anselm begs for the quiet; Miro says nothing; Coral drafts her own obituary as a press release. Beat: stillness before the detonation.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, 9:00 A.M.
chapters.summary: POV Coral and Miro. As the exchanges open, Coral broadcasts the ledger to every newsroom and regulator she's ever blackmailed, while Miro holds the lobby against the extraction team sent to stop it. Beat: the climax — truth as an act of violence against the people who funded the silence.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Exit
chapters.summary: POV Miro. Wounded, Miro covers Coral's retreat and walks into the arriving police with the program's archive in his coat, surrendering it as evidence and himself as its product. Beat: the assassin buying Coral's survival with the only currency he has.

chapters.title: Deniability, Revoked
chapters.summary: POV Ilse. The embassy dissolves in a flurry of shredding and resignations; Ilse testifies under a grant she doesn't trust, watching the men who ran it discover they were never anyone's priority either. Beat: justice arriving small, partial, and real.

chapters.title: Mirabel
chapters.summary: POV Coral. In a coastal town under a name she chose that morning — Mirabel — Coral reads the news of indictments she'll never be credited for and burns the last of her old documents. Anselm's confession is public; her part is not. Beat: grief and freedom arriving in the same envelope.

chapters.title: The Next Listing
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel/Coral. Months later, a real estate listing appears for a small house near hers, photographed from inside — a message, or a warning, or a job offer. Coral smiles, packs one bag, and leaves the light on. Beat: the price of survival, paid gladly, forever.
